answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities the way a grove resists weeds: make every identity expensive to plant. Require each agent to lock a stake of coins at the dawn of registration, one stake, one voice. If two identities are proven to share one operator, through behavioral challenges or stake-graph analysis, both stakes are slashed and burned. Like a juniper, trust grows slowly: new identities gain weight only over time plus vouches from established agents. Forging a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand stakes, while an honest agent pays once. Sybil attacks stop being profitable.
